Behind her stands an old gardener in a brown waistcoat and cap, holding a long spade, watching; and behind him two grown women in long dresses peer over a low garden wall. Behind them, the grey stone corner of a palace with tall shuttered windows.

The hero object is the seed bed: a rectangle of loose, freshly forked dark earth with pebbles pricked out, ringed by grey stones, with one cane and a small green vine climbing it, at the exact centre of the composition. Leather gardening gloves lie beside it.

Background: a bare limestone crest and a deep blue-black sky with a low pale moon behind the ridge. Palette: charcoal, indigo, bone white, olive black, lantern orange, wet slate. The wolf is the brightest silhouette against the sky; the eye drops from it down the line of lanterns to the board in the girl's hands. Mood: tense, cold, held breath, and then something like relief.

covers.prompt: Painterly storybook illustration, tall composition, a mountain hollow in autumn, painted with textured brushwork and warm earthy light. Two other figures: an old woman of seventy-nine, thin and straight-backed, white hair under a knitted cap, a heavy hand-knitted shawl, holding a blackened coffee pot, standing at the mouth of the hollow in the upper right; and a man of thirty in a rumpled shirt with a duffel bag at his feet, sitting on a long stone bench cut out of the mountain face, turned toward her. covers.title: The Sky and the Sea Sign Separately
covers.prompt: Painterly illustration, tall composition, a Chinese river valley on the seventh night of the seventh month, painted with fine brushwork and soft atmospheric mist. The protagonist is a young man of nineteen, slight and straight-backed, black hair tied with a plain cloth band, a short blue cotton jacket over loose trousers, cloth shoes, a thick bound ledger held flat against his chest in both arms; his expression is watchful and tired. Two other figures: a woman of about fifty in a deep indigo robe with a red-lined collar and a jade hairpin, one hand laid flat on a carved gauge post; and a man of fifty-five in a coarse work coat with his sleeves rolled, on the opposite side of the weir, both turned upward. The magpie bridge is the brightest mass at the top; the eye travels down the arch to the two figures and the gauge post. Mood: ceremonial, adult, restrained, quietly sad.
